intent: Moved sensors further forward and widened lateral spread to improve early line detection and lateral coverage, aiming to reduce line loss and stalls. Maintained sensor size at 0.016 m and wheel track at 0.12 m for turning agility. Kept body length at 0.20 m for stability and off-track tolerance. Expect these geometry changes to support the integrator's plan to reduce base speed to 1.1 and increase integral gain to 0.4, resulting in fewer stalls, better steady-state control, and improved race progress.
rationale: The previous iteration's geometry increased sensor size to 0.016 m, reduced wheel track to 0.12 m, and moved sensors slightly forward with a wider lateral spread to improve early line detection and turning agility. However, the latest race data still shows early stalls and multiple line loss events, indicating that while line sensing has improved, the robot struggles to maintain momentum and stable control. The integrator feedback recommends reducing base speed to 1.1 to prevent early stalls and increasing integral gain (ki) to 0.4 to improve steady-state error correction. To support these controller changes, I keep the sensor size at 0.016 m and maintain the wheel track at 0.12 m for turning agility. I move the sensors slightly further forward and widen their lateral spread a bit more within allowed limits to enhance early line detection and lateral coverage. The body length remains at 0.20 m to preserve stability and off-track tolerance, and the body width and mass remain unchanged to maintain handling balance. I expect these geometry adjustments combined with the integrator's controller tuning to reduce stalls and line loss events, improve progress, and enhance overall race performance.
